title: Former Yan
capsule: Former Yan (前燕) was a Xianbei state founded in 337 when Murong Huang, chieftain of the Murong clan in Liaoxi, took the title Prince of Yan, with his son Murong Jun formally declaring imperial rule in 352. From its successive capitals at Longcheng, Jicheng (Beijing), and finally Ye, Former Yan conquered Later Zhao's former territory and briefly dominated most of the North China Plain under the child emperor Murong Wei and his regent uncle Murong Ke. It fell in 370 when Former Qin under Fu Jian captured Ye and took Murong Wei prisoner — a state distinct from the ancient Warring-States-era kingdom of Yan that had vanished nearly six centuries earlier.
